paragraphs.source_en: Listen to my choking cry of grief; I implore it to my beloved god: Upon no mortal body on this earth, let there be any wound or scar! How can one of such pure and lofty spirit rise to heaven without passing through hell? ... My flesh has crossed the Mountain of Swords, been burnt upon the fire-tasting plank, and struggled over the Bridge of Nihil, all to pass the gates, so that today this bare, bare heart might stand, free and proud. Take this bare, bare heart, and have done with it, my beloved god! For besides you, there is no one to give him comfort and life; otherwise, you will grind him into powder and scatter him among the western clouds, but the color of his earnest devotion will forever tint your spring-morning new thoughts, and the dreams of autumn nights; Show mercy, my beloved god!
